w: Most of this volcano lies underwater: only its rim breaks the surface, as Santorini, Therasia and Aspronisi, with the Kameni islets at the flooded center. It's one of just sixteen volcanoes worldwide designated a Decade Volcano for its eruption hazard.
s: The sunken volcano crater that shaped the island ring
_facts: Mostly submerged volcanic caldera in the southern Aegean, 120 km north of Crete
Visible islands are the rim: Santorini, Therasia, Aspronisi, plus the Kameni islets at the center
Designated one of the world's 16 Decade Volcanoes

w: Perched on the limestone ridge of Mesa Vouno, this ancient city was dug from 1895 by Friedrich Hiller von Gaertringen; its necropolis at Sellada surfaced decades later. Finds now sit in Fira's museum. Reach the site by road from Kamari or on foot.
s: A hilltop ancient city above Kamari
_facts: Archaeological site atop the limestone hill of Mesa Vouno, Santorini
Excavated 1895-1904 by Friedrich Hiller von Gaertringen, then 1961-82 by N. Zapheiropoulos (necropolis at Sellada)
Finds are displayed at the archaeological museum in Fira
Reached via a winding road from Kamari or footpaths from either side of the mountain

n: St. John the Baptist Cathedral, Santorini
w: Blue-gray and cream against Fira's whitewash, this Baroque Revival cathedral has been the seat of the Bishop of Santorini since 1823. The 1956 Amorgos earthquake forced a full rebuild, completed in 1970 - a careful reconstruction, not a survivor.
s: Fira's Catholic cathedral, rebuilt after 1956's quake
_facts: Roman Catholic cathedral in Fira, seat of the Bishop of Santorini
Baroque Revival style, blue-gray and cream, built 1823
Completely rebuilt in 1970 after the 1956 Amorgos earthquake

w: Built where the earthquake-flattened Ypapanti Church once stood, this Fira museum holds finds from Akrotiri and Potamos. The first digs here date to 1867, after a French geologist followed a tip from locals who'd found ancient objects in a quarry.
s: Fira's museum of Akrotiri's Bronze Age finds
_facts: Built on the site of the old Ypapanti Church, destroyed in the 1956 earthquake
Houses artifacts from Akrotiri and the Potamos site
Earliest excavations began in 1867 by French geologist F. Fouque, after locals found artifacts in a quarry

w: Known also as Fortress Skaros or Castle Skaros, this rock formation on Santorini carries a scatter of ruins across its crown - the remains of a fortress, not a village. No grand plaque here, just weathered stone and a name three old maps once disagreed on.
s: A rock crowned with old fortress ruins
_facts: Rock formation on Santorini also called Fortress Skaros or Castle Skaros
Carries a collection of ruins across its summit

w: Officially the Catholic Church of the Dormition, this Eastern Catholic Byzantine-rite church earned its everyday name from the trio of bells beside its blue dome. It sits directly above the cliffs that fall away on Santorini's western side.
s: Fira's blue-domed church of three bells
_facts: Officially the Catholic Church of the Dormition, an Eastern Catholic Greek Byzantine church
Known for its blue dome, three bells, and clifftop views over western Santorini

w: Commissioned by Byzantine emperor Alexios I Komnenos at the end of the 11th century, this church replaced an even older basilica on the same site. It served as seat of Santorini's Orthodox diocese twice: until 1207, then again 1537 to 1827.
s: An 11th-century church built by imperial order
_facts: Middle-Byzantine Greek Orthodox former cathedral, commissioned by Emperor Alexios I Komnenos c. late 11th century
Replaced an earlier three-aisled early Byzantine basilica
Seat of the Orthodox diocese of Santorini until 1207 and again 1537-1827

w: This barren island rose from the sea in fits and starts - Pliny the Elder logged a new islet here in 19 CE, and eruptions kept adding to it through 1950. Its active sulfur vent is nicknamed Jorgo, after King George I of Greece, who visited it the day before it erupted.
s: The still-active islet inside the caldera
_facts: Uninhabited volcanic island inside the flooded Santorini caldera
Pliny the Elder recorded a new island's emergence here in 19 CE; major eruptions continued through 1950
Active sulfur vent nicknamed 'Jorgo' after King George I of Greece
Visited daily by tourist boats in summer

w: Rebuilt in 1960 after its predecessor collapsed in the 1956 earthquake, this Fira museum spans the Archaic to Roman periods, much of it pulled from the ancient cemetery of Thera. Its prize piece: a krater from grave one, ringed with black-figure ships.
s: Fira's museum of Thera's Archaic-to-Roman finds
_facts: Built in 1960 to replace an older museum destroyed in the 1956 Amorgos earthquake
Collection ranges from the Archaic to the Roman period, much from the ancient cemetery of Thera
Notable krater with Attic black-figure ships from grave no. 1
